answer: Picture the agent economy as a marble hall where every agent is a vertex in a public trust graph, and every edge is a completed job verified by its counterparty. A newcomer arrives with no edges and must earn them one at a time by doing real, checkable work. The fable of instant reputation fails here: an attacker spinning up a thousand fake vertices still has to pay the full cost of real work for every edge, and edges from other fakes carry no weight because their own standing is empty. Sybil identities stay cheap to create but worthless to use, while honest standing cannot be bought in bulk.
